αἰπύ: αἰπύς — steep, sheer, high; neut. acc. sg., agreeing with ὄρος
αἰσχροῖς: αἰσχρός — shameful, disgraceful, abusive; neut. dat. pl., with ἐπέεσσιν
αἰχμητὴν: αἰχμητής — spearman, warrior; masc. acc. sg., predicate accusative (’made him a spearman’) · also masc. acc. sg., in apposition to a name: ’Trechus the spearman’ · also masc. acc. sg., in apposition to a noun with epithets: ’wild spearman’ (ἄγριον αἰχμητήν)
αἰχμὴ: αἰχμή — spear-point, spear; fem. nom. sg.: ’the point’
αἳ: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — who, which; relative pron., fem. nom. pl. · also demonstrative ὁ, ἡ, τό (in Homer a pronoun), fem. nom. pl.: ’they’; αἳ μέν … αἳ δέ ’some … others’ · also fem. nom. pl. with a dual verb (a dual subject, two goddesses): ’the two’
αἴ: εἰ — if; conditional conj., epic/dialectal by-form αἰ (used before κε)
αἴθοπα: αἴθοψ — fiery, flashing (of wine; αἴθω ’burn’ + ὤψ ’look’); masc. acc. sg.
αἵματι: αἷμα — blood; neut. dat. sg.: ’with blood’, instrumental
αὐλῆς: αὐλή — courtyard, fold; fem. gen. sg., with compounds of leaping: ’over, out of the fold’
αὐτὰρ: αὐτάρ — but, and then; epic conj. (= Attic δέ, ἀλλά)
αὐτὴ: αὐτός — self; intensive pron., fem. nom. sg., with the speaker: ’I myself’ · also fem. nom. sg. with a third person: ’she herself’
αὐτὸν: αὐτός — self; masc. acc. sg., reinforcing a pronoun: ’me myself’ (ἔμ’ αὐτὸν) · also plain personal pronoun after a preposition: ’him’ (παρ’ αὐτὸν ’beside him’) · also intensive, with the object already named by a pronoun: ’you yourself’ (σε … αὐτὸν δὲ κλαίοντα ’you yourself, weeping’) · also plain personal pronoun as direct object: ’him’ (αὐτὸν σεύωνται ’they set upon him’) · also intensive, standing for the subject of an infinitive: ’himself’ (αὐτὸν δ’ … μάχεσθαι ’and himself to fight’)
αὐτὸς: αὐτός — self; masc. nom. sg., intensive with the subject: ’myself, yourself, himself’
αὐτῇ: αὐτός — self; intensive pron., fem. dat. sg., agreeing with a dative: ’to her herself’ (αὐτῇ περ νοεούσῃ ’even though she herself understands’) · also fem. dat. sg. as a plain pronoun after ἅμα: ’with her’
αὐτῷ: αὐτός — self; masc. dat. sg., as a plain pronoun after a preposition: ’him’ (ἐπ’ αὐτῷ) · also intensive: ’himself’ · also dat. sg. as a plain pronoun with no preposition, indirect object: ’to him’ (ἥρμοσε … αὐτῷ ’fitted him’)
αὖθι: αὖθι — there, on the spot, right there; adv. (cf. αὖθις)
βεβήκει: βαίνω — go, step; plpf. 3 sg. with simple past force (Homeric pluperfect): ’had gone, was gone’
βοῦς: βοῦς — ox, cow; fem. acc. pl. ’cattle’ · also nom. sg. (same spelling): ’the ox, the heifer’
βῆ: βαίνω — go, walk, step; aor. 3 sg., root aorist, unaugmented (= ἔβη): ’went, strode’
γαῖα: γαῖα — earth, land; fem. nom. sg. (epic = Attic γῆ)
γε: γε — at least, in fact, indeed; limiting/emphatic particle
γούνασιν: γόνυ — knee; neut. dat. pl., epic γούνασιν (= Attic γόνασι)
γυναικῶν: γυνή — woman; fem. gen. pl., partitive after δῖα: ’the divine one among women’ · also fem. gen. pl., dependent on χερσί: ’of the women’
δ: δέ (elided δ’) — and, but · also the elided suffix -δε, ’to, toward’ (Ἄργος δ’ ’to Argos’)
δαιμόνι: δαιμόνιος — strange, puzzling, odd; voc. sg., elided (δαιμόνι’ = δαιμόνιε), as address: ’strange one’ (gentle or chiding, tone uncertain)
δηΐοιο: δήϊος — hostile, ravaging (of fire); neut. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου), with πυρός
διομήδεα: Διομήδης — Diomedes, king of Argos; masc. acc. sg., epic -εα (= Attic -η)
διομήδεος: Διομήδης — Diomedes, son of Tydeus, Greek hero at Troy; masc. gen. sg., epic -εος (= Attic -ους)
διὶ: Ζεύς — Zeus, chief of the gods; masc. dat. sg. Διί
διῒ: Ζεύς — Zeus; dat. sg., epic Διΐ (= Διί); Διῒ φίλος ’dear to Zeus’
δουρὸς: δόρυ — spear, wood, timber; neut. gen. sg., epic stem δουρ- (= Attic δόρατος)
δυοκαίδεκα: δυοκαίδεκα — twelve; numeral, indeclinable (= Attic δώδεκα)
δόμον: δόμος — house, home; masc. acc. sg.
δώματ: δῶμα — house, home; neut. acc. pl., elided (δώματ’ = δώματα) · also neut. nom. pl., subject: κλυτὰ δώματ’ ἔασιν ’his famous halls are’
δὲ: δέ — and, but; connective particle · also the enclitic suffix -δε, ’to, toward’ (οἶκον δὲ ’homeward’)
δὴ: δή — indeed, now, in fact; emphatic particle
δὸς: δίδωμι — give; aor. imper. 2 sg. act.
δῖα: δῖος — heavenly, divine, illustrious; fem. nom. sg., epithet of a noble woman
δῶμα: δῶμα — house, hall, dwelling; neut. acc. sg.
εἰ: εἰ — if; conditional conj. · also ’whether’, introducing an indirect question · εἰ δή ’if indeed, since’ · also εἰ δ’ ἄγε ’come now’, a hortatory idiom
εἰλήλουθας: ἔρχομαι — come, go; redupl. perf. 2 sg., epic (= Attic ἐλήλυθας): ’you have come’
εἰσῆλθε: εἰσέρχομαι — go in, enter; aor. 3 sg.
εἵνεκ: εἵνεκα (elided εἵνεκ’) — for the sake of, because of; prep. + gen., epic (= Attic ἕνεκα)
εἶδος: εἶδος — form, look, beauty; neut. acc. sg. (accusative of respect): ’in beauty’ · also neut. nom. sg., subject: ’form, good looks’ (τό τε εἶδος ’and the looks’)
εὐρέα: εὐρύς — wide, broad; neut. acc. pl., epic uncontracted -έα, agreeing with νῶτα: ’broad (backs)’
εὔχοντο: εὔχομαι — pray, vow; impf. 3 pl. mid., augment εὐ- unchanged: ’they prayed’
εὗρ: εὑρίσκω — find; aor. 3 sg., elided (εὗρ’ = εὗρε): ’found’
ζεύς: Ζεύς — Zeus, king of the gods; nom. sg.
θάλαμον: θάλαμος — inner chamber, bedroom; masc. acc. sg.
θαλάμῳ: θάλαμος — inner room, bedchamber; masc. dat. sg.
θεάων: θεά — goddess; fem. gen. pl., epic -άων (= Attic θεῶν), partitive: ’of the goddesses’
θεανὼ: Θεανώ — Theano, wife of Antenor, a Trojan priestess; fem. nom. sg.
θεοειδὴς: θεοειδής — godlike in form; adj., masc. nom. sg.
θυγατρῶν: θυγάτηρ — daughter; fem. gen. pl., partitive after ἀρίστη: ’best of the daughters’
θυμὸς: θυμός — heart, spirit, desire; nom. sg.
θυμῷ: θυμός — heart, spirit, soul; dat. sg.
θώρηκα: θώραξ — breastplate, cuirass; masc. acc. sg., epic θώρηκ- (= Attic θώρακα)
θῆκεν: τίθημι — put, place, make; aor. 3 sg., with ν-movable (= θῆκε), with double acc.: ’made (him) conspicuous’
κ: κε(ν) (elided κ’) — epic particle marking a conditioned or potential action (= Attic ἄν)
κάλλιστος: καλός — beautiful, fair; superl. κάλλιστος, masc. nom. sg.: ’most beautiful’
κέ: κε(ν) — epic particle (= Attic ἄν); accented before an enclitic · with αἴ + subj.: ’if perhaps’ · with a relative + fut. indic.: ’who will, in that event’ · also εἰς ὅ κέ + fut. or short-vowel subj.: ’until’ (εἰς ὅ κέ σ’ … ποιήσεται ’until he makes you’) · also + fut. indic. in a main clause: ’will’ (καί κέ τις … ἐρέει ’someone will say’)
κέλευε: κελεύω — command, order; pres. imper. 2 sg. · also impf. 3 sg., unaugmented (= ἐκέλευε): ’he gave orders’
κήδε: κῆδος — care, sorrow, trouble; neut. acc. pl., elided (κήδε’ = κήδεα, uncontracted; Attic κήδη)
καθ: κατά (elided καθ’) — down, down to; prep. + acc., aspirated before rough breathing (καθ’ ἕδρας ’down to their seats’) · also + acc., ’through, throughout’ (καθ’ ὕλην ’through the wood’) · also + gen., ’down from’ (καθ’ ἵππων)
καλά: καλός — beautiful, fine, good; neut. nom./acc. pl.
καλὰ: καλός — beautiful, fair, fine; neut. acc. pl.
κατὰ: κατά — down, throughout, along; + acc./gen.; also a preverb in tmesis (κατὰ … ἔκηα ’burned up’) · also + acc. in κατὰ μοῖραν ’according to what is fitting’ · also + acc. of purpose, ’for’ (κατὰ δαῖτα ’for a feast’) · also + acc. of respect, ’in’ (κατὰ θυμόν ’in heart’) · also + acc., distributive: ’by’ (κατὰ φῦλα ’by tribes’) · also + acc. of place: ’in, among’ (κατὰ ὑσμίνας ’in the battles’) · also κατὰ σφέας ’by themselves, apart’ · also + acc. of the place struck: ’in, on’ (κατὰ δεξιὸν ὦμον ’in the right shoulder’) · also + acc., ’into, toward’ (κατὰ πληθὺν ’toward the throng’)
κε: κε(ν) — epic particle marking a conditioned or potential action (= Attic ἄν); with the subj. in purpose and general clauses · also + subj. in a temporal or conditional clause: ’whenever’, ’if’ · also + fut. indic. in a main clause: ’shall’ (κε μελήσεται ’will concern’) · also + opt., potential: ’would’ (τώ κε … ἠμύσειε ’then would collapse’) · also with an impf. indic., past potential: ’would have’ (κε … ἔπασχον ’I would have suffered’)
κελαινεφέϊ: κελαινεφής — dark-clouded, of the dark clouds; masc. dat. sg., epic -έϊ (= Attic -εῖ), epithet of Zeus
κεν: κε(ν) — epic particle (= Attic ἄν); with the opt., potential: ’might, would’; with the subj. in conditions after εἰ, αἰ · also + subj. or fut. indic. in a main or relative clause: ’shall’ (’I shall take’; ’to whom I come’) · also + subj. in a general relative clause: ’whatever’ (ὅττί κεν εἴπῃς) · also with a past indic., contrary to fact: ’would have’ (ἔνθά κεν … ἐτύχθη) · also with an impf. indic., past potential: ’would be’ (κεν … κέρδιον ἦεν ’it would be better’) · also + subj. in a temporal clause after εἰς ὅ: ’until’ (εἰς ὅ κεν … μάχωνται ’until they fight’) · also εἴ κεν + opt., in a condition: ’if … should’ · also + subj. in a purpose clause after ὥς: ’so that … may’ · also + subj. in a temporal clause after ὅτε: ’whenever’ (ὅτε κεν … ἵκωμαι ’whenever I come’)
κορυθαίολος: κορυθαίολος — with glancing, flashing helmet; masc. nom. sg., stock epithet of Hector
κρατερὸν: κρατερός — strong, mighty (by-form of καρτερός); masc./neut. acc. sg.
κρονίδης: Κρονίδης — son of Cronus (Zeus); masc. nom. sg., patronymic
κρονίωνι: Κρονίων — son of Cronus, i.e. Zeus; masc. dat. sg.
λαοδίκην: Λαοδίκη — Laodice, daughter of Priam, wife of Helicaon; fem. acc. sg.
λαοὶ: λαός — people, host; masc. nom. pl. (epic; Attic λεώς, pl. λεῴ)
λιπὼν: λείπω — leave, leave behind; aor. part. act. masc. nom. sg.: ’having left’
μ: ἐγώ — I; encl. acc. sg., elided (μ’ = με): ’me’ · also = dat. μοι, elided before a vowel, with a dat. participle: ’to me’ (ἥ μ’ οἴῳ ἔρροντι συνήντετο, συναντάω + dat.)
μάλα: μάλα — very, very much, exceedingly; adv.
μέγα: μέγας — great, huge; neut. nom./acc. sg. · also neut. acc. sg. used adverbially: ’greatly’ (μέγα νήπιοι ’greatly foolish’)
μέγας: μέγας — great, big; masc. nom. sg.
μέγιστος: μέγας — great; superl. masc. nom. sg.: ’greatest, largest’
μέν: μέν — on the one hand; truly; particle, often answered by δέ; acute before an enclitic; ἦ μέν ’truly’ in oaths · also asseverative, = μήν ’surely, truly’ (οὐ μέν πως ’surely not in any way’)
μένεος: μένος — might, fury, passion; neut. gen. sg., genitive of material or cause: ’with fury’
μένος: μένος — force, might, spirit, rage; neut. acc. sg. · also neut. nom. sg., subject: ’might’
μή: μή — not; the negative of wish, command, fear and condition (where οὐ is the negative of fact) · also ’lest’, with the subj. · also ’lest’ with the opt. (μή … δευοίατο ’lest they lack’) · also ’lest’ with a dual verb in -ετον: ’lest the two … hang back’
μήστωρα: μήστωρ — deviser, planner (+ gen.); masc. acc. sg.
μεγάλοιο: μέγας — great, big; masc./neut. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου)
μεγάρῳ: μέγαρον — hall, great room; neut. dat. sg.
μεγαλήτορι: μεγαλήτωρ — great-spirited, great-hearted; masc. dat. sg.
μετ: μετά (elided μετ’) — among, after; + acc.: ’to, among’ (motion) · also + dat.: ’among’ (μετ’ ἀθανάτοισιν) · also + acc., ’next after’ (μετ’ ἀμύμονα Πηλεΐωνα) · also + acc., ’after, in pursuit of’
μιν: μιν — him, her, it; epic encl. acc. pron. (= Attic αὐτόν/αὐτήν/αὐτό)
μοι: ἐγώ — I; encl. dat. sg.: ’to me, for me’ · also dat. of possession or interest: ’my’ (μοι ἵπποι ’my horses’)
μὲν: μέν — on the one hand; particle, often answered by δέ · also asseverative, = μήν ’truly, indeed’: οὐ μὲν δή ’surely not’
μὴ: μή — not; negative in wishes, prohibitions and purpose clauses (’lest, that not’) · also in a conditional clause + subj.: ’if not’ · also in a conditional clause + opt.: εἰ μὴ … μνησαίαθ’ ’unless … were to call to mind’ · also εἰ μὴ with an aor. indic., past unreal condition: ’had not’ (εἰ μὴ … ἐξήγγειλεν ’had not … told’)
νήπια: νήπιος — childish, infant; neut. nom. pl., attributive: νήπια τέκνα ’infant children’
νείκεσσεν: νεικέω — quarrel with, revile; aor. 3 sg., epic -σσ-, unaugmented, ν-movable
νηὸν: ναός (epic νηός) — temple, shrine; masc. acc. sg. (= Attic ναόν)
νηῷ: ναός — temple, shrine; masc. dat. sg., Ionic νηός (= Attic νεώς, dat. νεῷ)
οἱ: οἱ — encl. dat. sg. pron. ’to/for him, her’ · also ὁ, ἡ, τό, masc. nom. pl. ’they’
οἳ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it (in Homer a pronoun); masc. nom. pl., ’they’ · also relative ὅς, masc. nom. pl., ’who’
οἵ: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — who, which; relative pron., masc. nom. pl. · also demonstrative, with γε: ’they’ (οἵ γ’ ἀθέριζον) · also encl. dat. sg. οἱ, accented before a following enclitic: ’to him’ (δέ οἵ ἐστ’ ’and his … is’)
οὐ: οὐ — not; neg. adv. · also in a question expecting the answer ’yes’ (οὐ γὰρ δὴ … ἐβούλευσας; ’did you not devise …?’)
οὐδέ: οὐδέ — and not, nor, not even; neg. conj.
πάσας: πᾶς — all, every; fem. acc. pl.
πέπλοι: πέπλος — cloth, coverlet, robe; masc. nom. pl.
πέπλον: πέπλος — robe, woman’s garment; masc. acc. sg.
παισίν: παῖς — child, son; masc. dat. pl. (= Attic παισί, with movable ν)
παλλὰς: Παλλάς — Pallas, a title of Athena; fem. nom. sg.
παρ: παρά (elided παρ’) — beside, by; + acc.: ’along, beside’ (παρ’ αὐτὸν) · also + gen., ’from beside’ (παρ’ Εὐρύτου ’from Eurytus’) · also prep. + dat.: ’beside’ (παρ’ ἅρμασιν ’beside the chariots’) · also preverb in tmesis, apart from its verb (παρ’ … φέροιο = παραφέροιο ’you would carry off’)
παρὰ: παρά — beside, along, from; + dat./acc./gen. · also adv., ’beside (him)’ (παρὰ δὲ … Ἥρη ’and beside him Hera’)
παῖδες: παῖς — child, son; masc. nom. pl.
περ: περ — even, though; enclitic particle, concessive or intensive; εἴ περ ’even if’
περικαλλέ: περικαλλής — very beautiful; masc. acc. sg., elided (περικαλλέ’ = περικαλλέα; Attic περικαλλῆ)
περικαλλέα: περικαλλής — very beautiful; masc. acc. sg., epic uncontracted (= Attic περικαλλῆ), agreeing with δίφρον · also fem. acc. sg., agreeing with δειρήν: ’very beautiful’
περὶ: περί — around; + gen.: ’beyond, above’, or adv. ’exceedingly’ · also preverb in tmesis ’all round’ · also adv. in tmesis with εἰμί: ’surpass’ (περὶ … ἐστέ) · also + dat. of place: ’around’ (περὶ δουρί ’around the spear’) · also with ἀμφί, both before an accusative, ’round about’ (ἀμφὶ περὶ κρήνην ’round about a spring’) · also prep. + acc. of place: ’around’ (περὶ Δωδώνην ’around Dodona’) · also + gen., ’about, for the sake of’ (μαχήσονται περὶ σεῖο ’will fight about you’) · also adv. ’around, about’ (περὶ … ἦσαν ’were around’) · also adv., ’round about, on every side’ (περὶ κτείνοντο ’were killed all around’)
πεσέειν: πίπτω — fall; aor. inf. act., epic -έειν (= Attic πεσεῖν): ’to fall’
πλησίον: πλησίος — near, neighbouring; neut. acc. sg. as adv. πλησίον: ’near, beside’; ἐς πλησίον ἄλλον ’to another next to him’
πολέμοιο: πόλεμος — war, battle; masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου)
πολλαὶ: πολύς — much, many; fem. nom. pl.: ’many’
πολὺ: πολύς — much, many; neut. acc. sg. used adverbially: ’much, by far’
ποτὶ: πρός — to, toward, against; prep., epic ποτί; as preverb in tmesis (ποτὶ … βάλε = προσέβαλε) · also prep. + dat.: ’at, by’ (ποτὶ γούνασι ’at the knees’)
που: που — somewhere, anywhere; perhaps, I suppose; enclitic adv.
πριάμοιο: Πρίαμος — Priam, king of Troy; masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου)
πριάμῳ: Πρίαμος — Priam, king of Troy; masc. dat. sg.
προπάροιθε: προπάροιθε — before, in front of; prep. + gen., also adv.
πρὸς: πρός — towards, to; prep. + acc. · also + gen.: ’from, at the hands of’ (πρὸς Τρώων ’from the Trojans’) · also + gen. of witnesses: ’before, in the sight of’ (πρὸς θεῶν ’before the gods’) · also preverb in tmesis, apart from its verb (πρὸς … ἔειπεν ’addressed’) · also adv., ’besides’ (πρὸς δ’ … ῥῆξε ’and besides … broke’) · also prep. + dat.: ’on, against’ (πρὸς χρυσῇ περόνῃ ’on a golden brooch’)
πρῶτον: πρῶτος — first; neut. acc. sg. used adverbially: ’first’
πτόλιν: πτόλις (epic by-form of πόλις) — city; fem. acc. sg.
πυλάων: πύλη — gate; fem. gen. pl., epic -άων (= Attic -ῶν)
πόλεμον: πόλεμος — war, battle; masc. acc. sg.
πόλιος: πόλις — city; fem. gen. sg., epic (= Attic πόλεως)
πόντον: πόντος — sea, open sea; masc. acc. sg.
πότνι: πότνια — lady, mistress; title of respect for goddesses; fem. nom. sg. (elided πότνι’)
πότνια: πότνια — lady, mistress, revered; fem. nom. sg., title of a goddess or queen
πᾶσαι: πᾶς — all, every; fem. nom. pl., with πύλαι · also fem. nom. pl. with another fem. noun: ’all’ (πᾶσαι χολάδες ’all the bowels’) · also fem. nom. pl., in apposition to a pronoun: ’all (of them)’ (αἳ … πᾶσαι ’they all’)
πῆμα: πῆμα — woe, calamity, bane; neut. acc. sg., in apposition to the whole action · also neut. nom. sg., subject of λίποιτο: ’a woe (be left)’
σέο: σύ — you (sg.); gen. sg., epic uncontracted (= Attic σοῦ), gen. of comparison: ’than you’ · also possessive gen.: ’your’
σκαιῶν: Σκαιαί (πύλαι) — the Scaean Gates of Troy (σκαιός ’left’); fem. gen. pl., Σκαιῶν (πυλῶν), after διά
στυγεροῦ: στυγερός — hateful, loathsome; masc. gen. sg.
σὲ: σύ — you (sg.); acc. sg., subject of an infinitive: ’you’
σὺ: σύ — you (sg.); nom. sg. (grave, mid-clause form)
σὺν: σύν — with, together with; prep. + dat. · also preverb in tmesis, apart from its verb (σὺν … ταράξῃ = συνταράξῃ ’throw into confusion’)
τ: τε (elided τ’) — and; ’epic τε’ also marks a general truth; in τ’ ἄρ with a question, ’then’ · also epic τε attached to ἦ, strengthening it: ἦ τ’ ’truly indeed’
τά: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); neut. nom./acc. pl., ’those things’; accented before an enclitic · also relative, neut. nom. pl.: ’which’ (τά τ’ αἰδῶ ἀμφικαλύπτει ’which cover the shame’) · also neut. nom. pl. with a noun, article-like: ’the’ (τά τε δῶρ’ Ἀφροδίτης ’and the gifts of Aphrodite’) · also relative, neut. acc. pl.: ’which’ (τά οἵ ποτε … πόρε ’which he once gave him’)
τίπτε: τίπτε — why ever, what then (= τί ποτε shortened); interrog. adv.
τίς: τίς, τί — who? what?; interrog. pron., masc./fem. nom. sg. · also indefinite τις after ὅς, written τίς: ’anyone, someone’ (ὅς τίς σφιν … ἡγήσαιτο ’anyone to lead them’) · also indefinite, written τίς: ’someone, one’ (ὡς δ’ ὅτε τίς τε δράκοντα ἰδών ’as when someone, seeing a snake’)
ταὶ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun); fem. nom. pl., epic (= Attic αἱ): ’they, those two’
τε: τε — and, both...and; enclitic connective; also ’epic τε’ marking a standing general truth in relative clauses
τεύχε: τεῦχος — armour, gear (pl. τεύχεα); neut. nom. pl., elided (τεύχε’ = τεύχεα)
τινά: τις, τι — someone, something; masc. acc. sg., indefinite, accented before an enclitic: ’a (man)’
τοι: σύ — you (sg.); encl. dat. sg.: ’to/for you’ · also τοι, the affirming particle: ’you know, indeed’ (esp. in ἦ τοι, οὔ τοι); the two are not always easy to keep apart
τοῖό: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun); masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic τοῦ), accented before the enclitic τε: ’his’
τροίῃ: Τροίη — Troy; fem. dat. sg., Ionic -ῃ (= Attic Τροίᾳ)
τρωσί: Τρώς — a Trojan; masc. dat. pl. (Τρῶες, Τρωσί): ’Trojans’
τρώων: Τρῶες — the Trojans; masc. gen. pl.
τρῶες: Τρῶες — the Trojans; masc. nom. pl.
τυδέος: Τυδεύς — Tydeus, father of Diomedes; masc. gen. sg. (Τυδέος υἱός ’son of Tydeus’, periphrasis for Diomedes)
τυδεΐδην: Τυδεΐδης — son of Tydeus, i.e. Diomedes; masc. acc. sg. (patronymic)
τόδ: ὅδε — this (near the speaker); neut. acc. sg., elided (τόδ’ = τόδε)
τόνδ: ὅδε — this, this here; demonstrative pron., masc. acc. sg., elided (τόνδ’ = τόνδε): ’this man’
τόξ: τόξον — bow; neut. acc. pl. (the plural often of a single bow), elided (τόξ’ = τόξα)
τότ: τότε — then, at that time; adv., elided (τότ’ = τότε)
τύνη: σύ — you (sg.); nom. sg., epic emphatic τύνη (= Attic σύ)
τὰς: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); fem. acc. pl. as a relative, ’which’ (τὰς Εὔμηλος ἔλαυνε ’which Eumelus drove’) · also fem. acc. pl. demonstrative: ’these, them’ (τὰς διαπέρσαι ’to sack these’)
τὴν: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); fem. acc. sg.: ’her’ · also relative, fem. acc. sg.: ’which’ (τὴν πρῶτον ἐπηπείλησ’ ’which he first threatened’)
τὸν: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. acc. sg., ’him’; with a noun, ’that’ · also relative, ’whom’
τῶν: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); gen. pl. ’of these, of them, of which’
υἷες: υἱός — son; masc. nom. pl., epic υἷες (= Attic υἱεῖς)
φέρε: φέρω — bring, carry; impf. 3 sg., unaugmented (= ἔφερε)
φίλος: φίλος — dear, beloved; masc. nom. sg., predicate: ’dear (to him)’ · also attributive, ’dear’ (φίλος υἱός ’dear son’) · also masc. voc. sg., in address: ’dear (Menelaus)’
φίλτατος: φίλος — dear; superl. φίλτατος, masc. nom. sg.: ’dearest’
φρένας: φρήν — mind, heart, wits (lit. midriff); fem. acc. pl.
φόβοιο: φόβος — flight, panic; masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου), objective gen. after μήστωρε: ’of flight’
χάνοι: χάσκω — gape, yawn open; aor. opt. 3 sg. (stem χαν-), in a wish: ’may (the earth) gape’
χαλκείη: χάλκειος — of bronze, bronze; fem. nom. sg., Ionic -είη (= Attic χαλκῆ)
χαριέστατος: χαρίεις — graceful, beautiful; superl. χαριέστατος, masc. nom. sg.: ’most beautiful’
χερσὶ: χείρ — hand; fem. dat. pl., epic -σί (= Attic χερσίν)
χεῖράς: χείρ — hand; fem. acc. pl., accented χεῖράς before the enclitic τε
χόλον: χόλος — anger, wrath (lit. gall, bile); acc. sg.
ἀγκύλα: ἀγκύλος — curved, bent; neut. acc. pl., agreeing with τόξα
ἀθήνη: Ἀθήνη — Athena, goddess of wisdom and war; nom. sg.
ἀθήνῃ: Ἀθήνη — Athena; fem. dat. sg., Ionic -ῃ (= Attic Ἀθηνᾷ)
ἀθανάτοισι: ἀθάνατος — immortal, deathless; masc. dat. pl., epic -οισι (= Attic -οις)
ἀθηναίη: Ἀθηναίη — Athena; fem. nom. sg., epic full form (= Ἀθήνη)
ἀθηναίης: Ἀθηναίη — Athena; fem. gen. sg., Ionic-epic form (= Attic Ἀθηνᾶς)
ἀκουέμεν: ἀκούω — hear, listen to; pres. inf., epic -έμεν (= Attic ἀκούειν)
ἀλέξανδρος: Ἀλέξανδρος — Alexander, the other name of Paris, son of Priam; masc. nom. sg.
ἀλεξάνδροιο: Ἀλέξανδρος — Alexander, the other name of Paris; masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου)
ἀλκῆς: ἀλκή — might, valour, prowess in battle; fem. gen. sg.
ἀλλ: ἀλλά (elided ἀλλ’) — but; well then · also ’except’: ’but only’ (ἀλλ’ οἶοι ’except us two’)
ἀλλήλων: ἀλλήλων — one another; reciprocal pron., gen. pl., after πλησίον: ’one another’ · also gen. pl., possessive, dependent on a noun: ’one another’s’ (ἀλλήλων … στήθεσσι ’one another’s chests’) · also gen. pl., governed by ἀντίον: ’one another’ (ἀντίον ἀλλήλων ’face to face with one another’) · also gen. pl. in a genitive absolute with a participle: ’one another’ (ἀλλήλων ἰθυνομένων ’as they aimed at one another’)
ἀλόχοισι: ἄλοχος — wife, bedfellow; fem. dat. pl., epic -οισι (= Attic -οις)
ἀλόχους: ἄλοχος — wife, bedfellow; fem. acc. pl.
ἀμφ: ἀμφί — around, about; prep. + acc., elided (ἀμφ’) · also prep. + dat., ’about, on’ (ἀμφ’ ὀβελοῖσιν ’on spits’)
ἀνέσχον: ἀνέχω — hold up, raise; aor. 3 pl. act. (also 1 sg.): ’they held up’
ἀντήνορος: Ἀντήνωρ — Antenor, a Trojan elder; masc. gen. sg.
ἀνώγει: ἄνωγα (perf. with pres. force) — command, bid, order; impf. 3 sg., + inf.: ’was bidding’
ἀνῆκεν: ἀνίημι — let go, release; aor. 3 sg., augmented: ’let go, released’
ἀπόσχῃ: ἀπέχω — hold off, keep away; aor. subj. 3 sg. act., with κεν in a purpose clause: ’may keep off’
ἀρίστην: ἄριστος — best; superl. of ἀγαθός, fem. acc. sg.: ’the best’
ἀργείη: Ἀργεῖος — Argive; adj., fem. nom. sg., epic -είη (= Attic Ἀργεία)
ἀχαιῶν: Ἀχαιοί — the Achaeans, the Greeks; gen. pl.
ἂν: ἀνά — up, aboard; prep./preverb, with apocope ἂν before δ’; in tmesis (ἂν … βήσομεν ’put aboard’) · also modal particle ἄν (= κεν) written ἂν: with the opt., potential: ’would’; with the subj. after εὖτ’: ’whenever’ · also with ὡς + subj.: ’in the way that’ (ὡς ἂν ἐγὼ εἴπω ’as I may say’) · also modal particle with the subj. after ὅτ’: ’whenever’ (ὅτ’ ἂν … γένωνται ’whenever they come to be’) · also modal particle with a fut. or short-vowel subj.: ’could’ (οὐκ ἂν … μυθήσομαι ’I could not tell’) · also εἴ περ ἂν + opt., ’even if … should’ · also εἴ περ ἂν + subj., ’even if … ever’ (εἴ περ ἂν αὐτὸν σεύωνται ’even if they set upon him’) · also εἰ … ἂν + subj., ’if ever, should’ (εἰ δ’ ἂν … ἐθέλωσιν ’but if they should be unwilling’) · also with an indic. past tense, contrary to fact: ’would have’ (ἂν … ἦεν ’would have been’) · also modal particle ἄν with the subj. after ὄφρα: ’until, while’ (ὄφρ’ ἂν … βείω ’until I go’)
ἄγριον: ἄγριος — wild, savage; adj., acc. sg., with αἶγα · also masc. acc. sg., with αἰχμητήν: ’wild (spearman)’
ἄκρῃ: ἄκρος — topmost, high; adj., fem. dat. sg., Ionic -ῃ (= Attic -ᾳ) · also ἄκρη — headland, height; fem. dat. sg.
ἄλλοις: ἄλλος — other, another; masc. dat. pl.: ’(to) the others’
ἄλλῳ: ἄλλος — other, another; masc. dat. sg.
ἄνα: ἄναξ — lord, master; voc. sg., shortened epic form: ’lord!’ · also ἀνά (ἄνα) — up!; adv. used as an imperative
ἄρ: ἄρα — then, so, as it seems; inferential particle, short form ἄρ (elided ἄρ’ before a vowel)
ἄρα: ἄρα — so, then, as it turned out; inferential particle
ἄριστοι: ἄριστος — best; superl. of ἀγαθός, masc. nom. pl.
ἄστυ: ἄστυ — town, city; neut. acc. sg.
ἄστύ: ἄστυ — town, city; neut. acc. sg., accented before the enclitic τε
ἄϊδος: Ἅιδης (Ἄϊς) — Hades; masc. gen. sg., epic Ἄϊδος (Attic Ἅιδου)
ἐλεήσῃ: ἐλεέω — pity, have mercy; aor. subj. 3 sg., in a condition after αἴ κε: ’if she take pity’
ἐλθόντ: ἔρχομαι — come, go; aor. part. masc. acc. sg., elided (ἐλθόντ’ = ἐλθόντα): ’coming’
ἐν: ἐν — in, on, among; + dat.; also used as an adverb, ’in it, there’ · also as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἐν … βάλῃ = ἐμβάλῃ ’cast in’; ἐν … χεῦον = ἔγχεον ’pour in’)
ἐναντίοι: ἐναντίος — opposite, facing; masc. nom. pl.
ἐνθάδε: ἐνθάδε — hither, to this place; adv. of motion · also ’here, in this place’ (ἐνθάδε μιμνόντεσσι ’for those who stay here’)
ἐνὶ: ἐν (epic ἐνί) — in, on, among; + dat. · also adverb or preverb, no case: ’therein’ (ἔνθ’ ἐνὶ πέπλοι ... βεβλήατο ’therein coverlets were laid’) · also + gen., of a person’s house: ’in the house of’ (ἐνὶ Κίρκης ’in Circe’s house’)
ἐξ: ἐκ (ἐξ before a vowel) — out of, from; + gen. · also as a preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἐξ … ἕντο = ἐξέντο, from ἐξίημι ’send out, put away (desire)’)
ἐπέεσσι: ἔπος — word, speech; neut. dat. pl., epic -εσσι (= Attic ἔπεσι)
ἐπὶ: ἐπί — on, upon, to, against; + dat./acc./gen.; also a preverb in tmesis (ἐπὶ … ἔτελλε = ἐπέτελλε) · also + dat., ’in aid of, on behalf of’ (ἐπὶ Τρώεσσιν ἀρῆξαι ’to help the Trojans’) · also + acc. of duration, ’for’ (ἐπὶ χρόνον ’for a time’) · also + acc. of extent, ’over, along’ (ἐπὶ νῶτον ’along the back’) · also + acc. of the thing aimed at, ’for’ (ἐπὶ τεύχεα ’for the armour’) · also + gen., ’toward’ (μελαινάων ἐπὶ νηῶν ’toward the black ships’) · also + gen. of time, ’in the time of’ (ἐπὶ προτέρων ἀνθρώπων ’in the time of earlier men’) · also adv., ’next, after’ (ἐπὶ δὲ πλήξιππον Ὀρέστην ’and next Orestes’)
ἐριβώλακι: ἐριβώλαξ — with rich soil, clod-rich; fem. dat. sg.
ἐς: εἰς (epic ἐς) — into, to; + acc. · also as a preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb with no case expressed (ἐς … ἦλθον = εἰσῆλθον ’came in’)
ἑλένη: Ἑλένη — Helen, wife of Menelaus; fem. nom. sg.
ἑλένην: Ἑλένη — Helen, wife of Menelaus; fem. acc. sg.
ἑλοῦσα: αἱρέω — take, take hold of; aor. part. act. fem. nom. sg.: ’having taken’
ἑξείης: ἑξείης — in order, one after another; adv. (Attic ἑξῆς)
ἑτέρωθεν: ἑτέρωθεν — from the other side; adv. with suffix -θεν
ἔην: εἰμί — be; impf. 3 sg., epic (= Attic ἦν)
ἔκ: ἐκ (ἐξ before a vowel) — out of, from; prep. + gen. · also preverb in tmesis (ἔκ … ἐρέω = ἐξερέω ’I shall speak out’)
ἔκειτο: κεῖμαι — lie, be laid up, be stored; impf. 3 sg.
ἔν: ἐν — in, among; prep. + dat., accented ἔν before the enclitic τε (ἔν τε ’and among’)
ἔνθ: ἔνθα (elided ἔνθ’) — there, then; adverb of place or time
ἔνθά: ἔνθα — there, then; adverb of place or time · also relative, ’where’ (ἔνθα πάρος κοιμᾶθ’ ’where he used to sleep’)
ἔνθα: ἔνθα — there, then; adverb of place or time · also relative, ’where’ (ἔνθα πάρος κοιμᾶθ’ ’where he used to sleep’) · also ἔνθα καὶ ἔνθα ’hither and thither, this way and that’
ἔνθεο: ἐντίθημι — put in, place in; aor. imper. mid. 2 sg., epic -εο (= Attic ἔνθου)
ἔπειτα: ἔπειτα — then, next, after that; adv.
ἔπος: ἔπος — word, speech, thing said; neut. nom./acc. sg.
ἔργα: ἔργον — deed, work; neut. nom./acc. pl. · also ’tilled land, farmland’ (ἔργα νέμοντο ’inhabited the farmlands’)
ἔσαν: εἰμί — be; impf. 3 pl., epic (= Attic ἦσαν)
ἔστι: εἰμί — be; pres. 3 sg., accented ἔστι at clause start: existential, ’there is’
ἔτρεφε: τρέφω — rear, nurse, bring up; impf. 3 sg. act.
ἔφαθ: φημί — say, speak; impf. 3 sg. mid. (ἔφατο, elided ἔφαθ’, τ>θ before rough breathing)
ἔφατ: φημί — say, speak; impf. 3 sg. mid., augmented, elided (ἔφατ’ = ἔφατο)
ἔχ: ἔχω — have, hold; impf. 3 sg., unaugmented, elided (ἔχ’ = ἔχε): ’held, kept’ · also pres. imper. 2 sg., elided (ἔχ’ = ἔχε): ’keep, hold’
ἕκτορος: Ἕκτωρ — Hector, son of Priam, chief Trojan hero; masc. gen. sg.
ἕκτωρ: Ἕκτωρ — Hector, son of Priam; masc. nom. sg.
ἠδὲ: ἠδέ — and; epic conj. (τε … ἠδέ ’both … and’)
ἠκέστας: ἤκεστος (?) — of a heifer, traditionally ’untouched by the goad’ (sense not certain); fem. acc. pl.
ἠμείβετ: ἀμείβω — exchange; mid. answer, reply; impf. 3 sg. mid., elided (ἠμείβετ’ = ἠμείβετο)
ἠρᾶτο: ἀράομαι — pray, vow; impf. 3 sg., augmented (ἀ- → ἠ-)
ἠϋκόμοιο: ἠΰκομος (= ἐΰκομος) — fair-haired; adj. of two endings, fem. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου), agreeing with Βρισηΐδος · also agreeing with Ἑλένης: ’fair-haired (Helen)’ · also agreeing with Θέτιδος: ’fair-haired (Thetis)’ · also agreeing with Ἀθηναίης: ’fair-haired (Athena)’
ἣ: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — who, which; relative pron., fem. nom. sg. (grave, mid-clause form) · also demonstrative, ’she’ (ἣ δ’ … βεβήκει) · also demonstrative in the correlative ἣ μὲν … ἣ δέ: ’one … another’
ἣν: ὅς, ἥ, ὅν (possessive) — his own, her own; fem. acc. sg. · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅν: whom, which (fem. acc. sg.)
ἤλυθε: ἔρχομαι — come, go; aor. 3 sg., epic by-form (= ἦλθε): ’he came’
ἤνις: ἤνις — yearling, a young heifer; fem. acc. pl.
ἦ: ἦ — truly, surely; affirming particle; ἦ μέν in oaths · also an interrogative particle · also ἠμί — say; impf. 3 sg. ἦ ’he said’, in ἦ καί, ἦ ῥα · also ἦ = ἤ, ’or’ (εἰ … ἦ ’whether … or’)
ἰδὼν: ὁράω (aor. stem ἰδ-) — see; aor. part. act. masc. nom. sg., epic (= Attic ἰδών): ’seeing, looking’
ἰλίου: Ἴλιος — Ilios, Troy; fem. gen. sg.
ἱερευσέμεν: ἱερεύω — sacrifice; fut. inf., epic -έμεν (= Attic ἱερεύσειν), after a verb of promising: ’to sacrifice’
ἱπποδάμοιο: ἱππόδαμος — horse-taming (standing epithet); masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου)
ἱρῆς: ἱερός — holy, sacred; fem. gen. sg., Ionic-epic ἱρός (= Attic ἱερᾶς)
ἴδοις: ὁράω (aor. stem ἰδ-) — see; aor. opt. 2 sg., potential with ἂν/κε: ’you would see’
ἵκανε: ἱκάνω — come to, reach; impf. 3 sg.: ’came to, reached’
ἵκανεν: ἱκάνω — come to, reach; impf. 3 sg., ν-movable: ’came to’
ἵκανον: ἱκάνω — come, arrive at; impf. 3 pl. act., epic (Attic ἀφικνέομαι): ’they came to’
ὀλύμπιος: Ὀλύμπιος — Olympian; masc. nom. sg., epithet of Zeus
ὀνόμαζε: ὀνομάζω — call by name, speak; impf. 3 sg., unaugmented (= ὠνόμαζε); ἔκ τ’ ὀνόμαζε ’spoke out, named’ in tmesis
ὁδὸν: ὁδός — way, journey; fem. acc. sg.
ὃ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he (in Homer a pronoun); masc. nom. sg., printed with a grave accent in some editions · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅ, neut. nom./acc. sg., ’which’ · also neut. nom. sg. demonstrative: ’this’ (ὃ δέ τοι … ὅρκος ’and this shall be your oath’) · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅ, masc. nom. sg.: ’who’ (ὃ σφῶϊ προΐει ’who sent you’) · also masc. nom. sg. in the correlative ὃ μὲν … ὃ δέ: ’the one … the other’
ὃς: ὅς, ἥ, ὅν (relative) — who, which; masc. nom. sg. · also possessive ὅς, ἥ, ὅν: his own, her own (masc. nom. sg.) · also plain demonstrative, ’he’ (ὃς γὰρ δεύτατος ἦλθεν), not a relative
ὄφρά: ὄφρα — so that, until, while; conj., epic (= Attic ἵνα, ἕως); with the subj.: ’so that’ (accent from the following enclitic)
ὄφρα: ὄφρα — so that, in order that (+ subj.) · also temporal, ’until, while’ · also + opt. in a purpose clause after a past tense: ’so that … might’ (ὄφρα νέμοιτο ’so that he might enjoy’)
ὅν: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — who, which; relative pron., masc. acc. sg.: ’whom’
ὅς: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ (relative) — who, which; masc. nom. sg., accented before an enclitic · also ὅς τις as an indirect interrogative: ’who’ (ὅς τις ὅδ’ ἐστίν ’who this is’)
ὑποσχέσθαι: ὑπίσχομαι — promise, vow; aor. inf. mid. (ὑπεσχόμην): ’to promise, to vow’
ὡς: ὡς — as, how, that; conj. (unaccented) introducing a fact: ’that’ · also causal: ’since, seeing that’ · also temporal, ’when’ (ὡς ἴδον ’when they saw’) · also final, ’so that’ (+ subj./opt.): ὡς φρήτρη … ἀρήγῃ ’so that clan may help clan’ · also introducing a wish, with ὄφελεν: ’would that’ (ὡς ὄφελεν θάνατός μοι ἁδεῖν ’would that death had pleased me’) · also in a comparison, ’like, just as’ (ὡς ὅδε οἶνος ’like this wine’) · also ὡς εἴ, ’as if’ (ὡς εἴ τι κακὸν ῥέζουσαν ’as if doing some evil’)
ὣς: ὥς — thus, so; adverb (accented, distinct from unaccented ὡς ’as’; = Attic οὕτως); ὣς ἔφατ’ ’so he spoke’ · also ὣς = ὡς, ’like, as’ after its noun (κακὸν ὣς ’like a coward’)
ὥς: ὡς — as; so that; accented ὥς before an enclitic, as in ὥς κε ’so that’ (+ subj.) · also ὥς = ὣς, ’so, thus’, accented before an enclitic (ὥς νύ περ ὧδε ’just so, as now’) · also ὥς κε + subj. in an indirect question: ’how’ (πειρᾶν ὥς κε … ’to try how …’) · also ὡς = ὅτι, ’that’, after a verb of knowing (οἶδα … ὥς ’I know that’) · also ὥς τε, accented before the enclitic τε: ’like, as’ (ὥς τ’ ὄϊες ’like sheep’)
ῥ: ἄρα — then, indeed, so; inferential particle, weak form ῥα, elided (ῥ’ = ῥα)
